title: Dualizability detected by jointly conservative closed monoidal functors
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ and $(\mathcal D_i)_{i\in I}$ be symmetric monoidal categories: monoidal categories [def-sfb-monoidal-category] with a symmetry, that is, isomorphisms $\sigma_{A,B}:A\otimes B\xrightarrow{\sim}B\otimes A$ natural in both variables with $\sigma_{B,A}\circ\sigma_{A,B}=1$ and $\alpha_{B,C,A}\circ\sigma_{A,B\otimes C}\circ\alpha_{A,B,C}=(1_B\otimes\sigma_{A,C})\circ\alpha_{B,A,C}\circ(\sigma_{A,B}\otimes1_C)$, $\alpha$ the associator. Assume that each category has chosen internal-Hom objects $[A,B]$ and natural tensor--internal-Hom adjunction bijections
$$\operatorname{Hom}(A\otimes B,C)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(A,[B,C]),$$
whose value at a morphism is called its transpose. Let $F_i:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D_i$ be strong symmetric monoidal functors: strong monoidal functors [def-sfb-strong-monoidal-functor] whose tensorators $\mu_{A,B}:F_iA\otimes F_iB\xrightarrow{\sim}F_i(A\otimes B)$ satisfy $F_i(\sigma_{A,B})\circ\mu_{A,B}=\mu_{B,A}\circ\sigma_{F_iA,F_iB}$. Suppose the family is jointly conservative: a morphism $a$ of $\mathcal C$ is an isomorphism whenever every $F_i(a)$ is an isomorphism. For each $i$ assume a natural isomorphism $h_i(A,B):F_i([A,B])\xrightarrow{\sim}[F_iA,F_iB]$ such that the tensor--internal-Hom adjunctions are preserved: for every $g:A\otimes B\to C$, the transpose of $F_i(g)\circ\mu_{A,B}:F_iA\otimes F_iB\to F_iC$ is $h_i(B,C)\circ F_i(\tilde g)$, where $\tilde g:A\to[B,C]$ is the transpose of $g$. Then, for an object $K$ of $\mathcal C$, $K$ is dualizable (there are an object $D$, evaluation $D\otimes K\to\mathbf1$ and coevaluation $\mathbf1\to K\otimes D$ satisfying both triangle identities) if and only if every $F_i(K)$ is dualizable in $\mathcal D_i$. The index set $I$ may be empty or infinite.

source.place: Lemma 4.5 proof: monoidal, conservative, and internal-Hom properties imply locality of lisse objects

proof.text:
First prove preservation. Given duality data $E,a,b$ for $K$, fix $i$, write $F=F_i$, and let $s:\mathbf1_i\xrightarrow{\sim}F\mathbf1$ be its unit comparison. Set
$$a_i=s^{-1}\circ F(a)\circ\mu_{E,K},\qquad b_i=\mu_{K,E}^{-1}\circ F(b)\circ s.$$
These are maps $FE\otimes FK\to\mathbf1_i$ and $\mathbf1_i\to FK\otimes FE$. Substitute these formulas into each triangle composite. Tensorator naturality moves $F(a)$ and $F(b)$ together; the associativity and unit equations in [def-sfb-strong-monoidal-functor] cancel the intervening tensorators and $s,s^{-1}$. The two composites become respectively $F((1_K\otimes a)(b\otimes1_K))=1_{FK}$ and $F((a\otimes1_E)(1_E\otimes b))=1_{FE}$, with the associators and unitors of [def-sfb-monoidal-category] included on each side. Thus $FE,a_i,b_i$ are duality data for $FK$. This direction uses neither conservativity nor preservation of internal Hom.

source.place: Tag 0FFP, definition-dual and the observation immediately following it; Tag 0FFL, definition-functor-monoidal-categories

proof.text:
For reflection put $D=[K,\mathbf1]$ and let $\epsilon:D\otimes K\to\mathbf1$ be the inverse transpose of $1_D$. For every object $M$ define $\varphi_M:M\otimes D\to[K,M]$ to be the transpose of
$$(M\otimes D)\otimes K\xrightarrow{\alpha_{M,D,K}}M\otimes(D\otimes K)\xrightarrow{1_M\otimes\epsilon}M\otimes\mathbf1\xrightarrow{\rho_M}M.$$
For any objects $A,B$ write $\operatorname{ev}_{A,B}:[A,B]\otimes A\to B$ for the inverse transpose of $1_{[A,B]}$. Naturality of the given Hom bijections says that the inverse transpose of $t:T\to[A,B]$ is $\operatorname{ev}_{A,B}\circ(t\otimes1_A)$. All associators, unitors and tensor compositions used here are those of [def-sfb-monoidal-category].

source.place: Lemma 4.5, lisse part of the proof; explicit canonical evaluation comparison

proof.text:
Fix $i$, put $L=F_iK$, and choose a dual $E$ of $L$ with evaluation $a:E\otimes L\to\mathbf1_i$ and coevaluation $b:\mathbf1_i\to L\otimes E$. By [lem-sfb-dual-tensor-adjunctions], $-\otimes E$ is right adjoint to $-\otimes L$. Normalize this adjunction by the dual-pair bijection
$$f:A\otimes L\to M\ \longmapsto\ (f\otimes1_E)\circ(1_A\otimes b),\qquad t\longmapsto(1_M\otimes a)\circ(t\otimes1_L).$$
Here and below in this step the canonical associators and unitors are suppressed, as in [def-sfb-monoidal-category]. Composing the displayed formulas in either order cancels $b$ against $a$ by the corresponding triangle identity, so its counit at $M$ is $1_M\otimes a$. Apply [det-sp-unique-right-adjoint] to this adjunction and the given internal-Hom adjunction. It gives isomorphisms $\theta_M:M\otimes E\xrightarrow{\sim}[L,M]$ whose inverse transposes are $1_M\otimes a$. In particular $q=\theta_{\mathbf1_i}\circ\lambda_E^{-1}:E\xrightarrow{\sim}[L,\mathbf1_i]$ satisfies $\operatorname{ev}_{L,\mathbf1_i}(q\otimes1_L)=a$. Let $\varphi^i_M:M\otimes[L,\mathbf1_i]\to[L,M]$ be the evaluation comparison defined as in step 2 in $\mathcal D_i$. Taking inverse transposes of both sides gives
$$\varphi^i_M\circ(1_M\otimes q)=\theta_M.$$
Indeed both inverse transposes are $1_M\otimes a$, followed by the right unitor. Thus $\varphi^i_M=\theta_M\circ(1_M\otimes q^{-1})$ is an isomorphism for every $M\in\mathcal D_i$.

source.place: Tag 0FFQ, lemma-left-dual (including its displayed Hom maps); Tag 0FFR, remark-left-dual-adjoint; right-adjoint uniqueness as stated in det-sp-unique-right-adjoint

proof.text:
Fix $i$ again, write $F=F_i$, and retain its unit comparison $s:\mathbf1_i\xrightarrow{\sim}F\mathbf1$. Define the isomorphism
$$u_i:FD\xrightarrow{h_i(K,\mathbf1)}[FK,F\mathbf1]\xrightarrow{[FK,s^{-1}]}[FK,\mathbf1_i].$$
The compatibility of transposes assumed in the statement, applied to $\epsilon$ (whose transpose is $1_D$), and naturality in the target $s^{-1}$, gives the exact evaluation identity
$$\operatorname{ev}_{FK,\mathbf1_i}\circ(u_i\otimes1_{FK})=s^{-1}\circ F(\epsilon)\circ\mu_{D,K}.$$
This specifies the comparison on the actual evaluation, including the unit factor. The map $[FK,s^{-1}]$ is invertible because its inverse is $[FK,s]$; hence $u_i$ is invertible. This uses only the assumed internal-Hom functoriality and [def-sfb-strong-monoidal-functor], with tensor notation from [def-sfb-monoidal-category].

source.place: Lemma 4.5 proof, internal-Hom preservation in the lisse argument; explicit transpose calculation

proof.text:
For every $M\in\mathcal C$, the precise comparison of the canonical maps is
$$h_i(K,M)\circ F_i(\varphi_M)\circ\mu_{M,D}=\varphi^i_{F_iM}\circ(1_{F_iM}\otimes u_i).$$
To check it, take inverse transposes in $\mathcal D_i$. By the assumed transpose compatibility, the inverse transpose on the left is $F_i(\rho_M(1_M\otimes\epsilon)\alpha_{M,D,K})$, precomposed with $\mu_{M\otimes D,K}\circ(\mu_{M,D}\otimes1_{F_iK})$. The associativity and right-unit equations and tensorator naturality of [def-sfb-strong-monoidal-functor] rewrite this as
$$\rho_{F_iM}\circ\bigl(1_{F_iM}\otimes(s^{-1}F_i(\epsilon)\mu_{D,K})\bigr)\circ\alpha_{F_iM,F_iD,F_iK}.$$
Using the evaluation identity in step 4, this is exactly the inverse transpose of the right side. Injectivity of the transpose bijection proves the displayed comparison. Associators and unitors have the directions fixed by [def-sfb-monoidal-category].

source.place: Lemma 4.5 proof, monoidal and internal-Hom properties in the lisse argument; canonical-map compatibility

proof.text: Every factor on the right of the comparison in step 5 is an isomorphism, by steps 3 and 4. Its two outer factors $h_i(K,M)$ and $\mu_{M,D}$ on the left are isomorphisms by hypothesis. Composing their inverses shows that $F_i(\varphi_M)$ is an isomorphism for every $i$. Joint conservativity therefore makes $\varphi_M$ an isomorphism, in particular $\varphi_K$. This reasoning applies unchanged to an infinite index set. If $I$ is empty, the assumption of joint conservativity itself says every morphism of $\mathcal C$ is an isomorphism, so it still applies to $\varphi_K$.

source.place: Lemma 4.5 proof, conservative functor in the lisse argument; jointly conservative family version

proof.text:
Let $j:\mathbf1\to[K,K]$ be the transpose of $\lambda_K:\mathbf1\otimes K\to K$, and set $c=\varphi_K^{-1}\circ j:\mathbf1\to K\otimes D$. Untranspose $\varphi_K\circ c=j$. By step 2 and naturality in the first variable, this gives
$$\rho_K\circ(1_K\otimes\epsilon)\circ\alpha_{K,D,K}\circ(c\otimes1_K)=\lambda_K.$$
Precompose by $\lambda_K^{-1}$. The resulting equality is precisely the $K$-triangle for $\epsilon,c$. These are substitutions into the stated adjunction bijection, using only the monoidal constraints of [def-sfb-monoidal-category].

source.place: Tag 0FFP, definition-dual, first triangle; direct inverse-transpose calculation

proof.text:
For the second triangle put $g=(\epsilon\otimes1_D)\circ(1_D\otimes c):D\to D$, suppressing the canonical associator and unitors of [def-sfb-monoidal-category]. Bifunctoriality of tensor gives
$$\epsilon\circ(g\otimes1_K)=\epsilon\circ(\epsilon\otimes1_D\otimes1_K)\circ(1_D\otimes c\otimes1_K)=\epsilon\circ(1_D\otimes1_K\otimes\epsilon)\circ(1_D\otimes c\otimes1_K)=\epsilon.$$
The middle equality says that contracting the two disjoint $D\otimes K$ pairs in either order is the same morphism $\epsilon\otimes\epsilon$, followed by $\mathbf1\otimes\mathbf1\cong\mathbf1$; the final equality is the $K$-triangle of step 7. Under the given transpose bijection $\operatorname{Hom}(D\otimes K,\mathbf1)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(D,D)$, the first and last morphisms correspond to $g$ and $1_D$, since the transpose of $\epsilon$ is $1_D$. Thus $g=1_D$, which is the $D$-triangle. Consequently $D,\epsilon,c$ are duality data for $K$, proving reflection and the equivalence.

source.place: Tag 0FFP, definition-dual, second triangle; direct bifunctoriality and adjunction calculation

lean.statement: theorem dualizable_iff_of_jointly_conservative {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C] [MonoidalCategory C] [SymmetricCategory C] [MonoidalClosed C] {I : Type w} (D : I → Type u') [∀ i, Category.{v'} (D i)] [∀ i, MonoidalCategory (D i)] [∀ i, SymmetricCategory (D i)] [∀ i, MonoidalClosed (D i)] (F : ∀ i, C ⥤ D i) [∀ i, (F i).Monoidal] (hSymmetry : ∀ (i : I) (A B : C), Functor.LaxMonoidal.μ (F i) A B ≫ (F i).map (β_ A B).hom = (β_ ((F i).obj A) ((F i).obj B)).hom ≫ Functor.LaxMonoidal.μ (F i) B A) (hConservative : ∀ {A B : C} (a : A ⟶ B), (∀ i : I, IsIso ((F i).map a)) → IsIso a) (h : ∀ (i : I) (B : C), ihom B ⋙ F i ≅ F i ⋙ ihom ((F i).obj B)) (hHomNaturality : ∀ (i : I) {A B : C} (f : A ⟶ B) (T : C), (F i).map ((pre f).app T) ≫ (h i A).hom.app T = (h i B).hom.app T ≫ (pre ((F i).map f)).app ((F i).obj T)) (hTranspose : ∀ (i : I) (A B T : C) (g : A ⊗ B ⟶ T), curry ((β_ ((F i).obj B) ((F i).obj A)).hom ≫ Functor.LaxMonoidal.μ (F i) A B ≫ (F i).map g) = (F i).map (curry ((β_ B A).hom ≫ g)) ≫ (h i B).hom.app T) (K : C) : (∃ E : C, Nonempty (ExactPairing K E)) ↔ ∀ i : I, ∃ E : D i, Nonempty (ExactPairing ((F i).obj K) E)
